html:
A battle at Himera, on the north coast of Sicily, in 480 BCE, in which the Greek tyrants Gelon of Syracuse and Theron of Akragas destroyed a large army of Carthage.

Carthage had come to restore an ally Theron had driven out of Himera. Its general Hamilcar was killed, and his army was wiped out or captured. Carthage paid a large sum in silver, and the prisoners were put to work on temples in the Greek cities.

Greeks later claimed it was fought on the same day as the Battle of Salamis; Herodotus reports this, and others tied it to Thermopylae. It made a good story of Greeks beating barbarians east and west at once, but there is no evidence the two attacks were planned together.

The victory made Syracuse the leading power of Greek Sicily. Carthage stayed out of the Greek part of the island for about seventy years, until it came back and destroyed Himera in 409 BCE.
sum: A battle at Himera, on the north coast of Sicily, in 480 BCE, in which the Greek tyrants Gelon of Syracuse and Theron of Akragas destroyed a large army of Carthage.
